# Independent audit: original critical residual-row Jensen failure


`candidate d51bf499e3dcaeba`.
Result: **PASS**. No correction identified.

The radii 1/2,1,5/4 have decreasing successive slopes, so their
piecewise-linear interpolant is concave. The lifted convex hull has
exactly the three stated interval fibers and no other integer base.
Its masses 1,2,5/2 sum to 11/2, and all are strictly less than M/2.

The proof at (0,0) retains every nonvertical direction after positive
normalization and x-reflection. The endpoint tail sum equals
5/2-[T_(5/4)(a)-T_(1/2)(a)]. The difference is the tail length of
the larger interval outside the smaller one, hence is at most3/2.
The own fiber adds one, proving the all-halfspace lower bound2.
Pure integer through-point caps have at least mass3 and explicitly
retain their whole boundary fiber.

For L>=5/4 each stated cap contains the full left interval, one
middle half, and zero length on the right. Their middle cover gives
the matching upper bound2 on that fiber; finite integer tilts
isolate any endpoint own cap and yield maxima1/2 and5/4 there.
The shorter middle own-side cap plus the fully included left fiber
has mass2-|x| for x!=0, proving the asserted uniqueness. Thus the
selected caps are truly critical at the global deepest point.

The added right-cover cap thresholds are correct at every base:
at the right they cut at plus/minus1/4, giving masses3/2; at the
other two bases they are strictly empty. The four original caps
cover the actual source and give obstacle vector (0,1,1).
The linear majorant objective is at least3h_0>=3, and the constant
height vector attains3. The source correctly does not claim uniqueness.

The stated convexity flows have zero displacement at source0.
Their stationarity is lambda_0=1+2=3 and lambda_-=lambda_+=1-1=0.
The constant supporting slopes and complementary slackness are
valid, so this is an actual KKT row, not a separately chosen
arithmetic coupling. Its absorbing chain stops at each of the
three destinations with exactly probability1/3.

For the chosen cap, the actual residual lengths are (0,1,5/2),
and its source is active because f_H(0)=h_0=e_0=1. Their ORIGINAL
row average is exactly7/6>1. This is therefore a genuine failure
of the unchanged residual-root comparison, as distinguished from
the earlier example where only a geometric first-exit bound was
unnecessarily large.

The critical-menu exhaustion is exact. Equality in the endpoint
tail lower bound requires capturing both outer pieces of the
larger interval, which happens precisely at a<=-5/4. Reflection
gives the other continuous-normal sign, and purely integer caps
are not critical. At equality of a supporting threshold a captured
endpoint singleton has zero length, so every such critical cap
still has the same residual array. A cap strictly containing the
deepest point cannot also have mass2, since shifting its boundary
toward the point removes a positive middle strip. Thus no omitted
critical containing cap repairs the fixed row.

The source remains above the OC target: Q/M=4/11>1/4. It disproves
the unconditional active-row claim and any repair by selecting a
different critical cap for this SAME row. It does not exclude other
KKT choices or transport rows, or a theorem with an essential
strictly below-target hypothesis.

An independent Fraction-only diagnostic checked all tail inequalities
and the exact critical-tilt equivalence at321 rational slopes, plus
the KKT, Jensen and mass constants. Together with the companion slab
audit's dimension checks, the run passed1545 exact checks. The full
menu classification is the analytic tail argument above, not a
conclusion inferred from that finite sample.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
